lesson.title: React useEffect() Hook: Mount, Dependencies and Cleanup
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

sources.title: React useEffect() Hook: Mount, Dependencies and Cleanup

steps.title: Build a counter component
steps.instructions: Scaffold a Vite React app (npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react, npm install, npm run dev) and create src/MyComponent.jsx rendered from App.jsx, importing useState and useEffect. Add a count state starting at 0, a paragraph `Count: {count}`, and an Add button whose addCount calls setCount(c => c + 1).

targets.caption: count state starting at 0
Handler that adds one to count
Rendered counter paragraph

explanations.topic: Importing useEffect alongside useState from React
Creating a count state variable and its setter with initial value 0
Using an updater function with the previous state to add one

hints: Start with the import: you need both hooks from the 'react' package inside curly braces.

Destructure the state: const [count, setCount] = useState(0); then render

Count: {count}

.
Give the button onClick={addCount} (no parentheses) and declare function addCount() that calls setCount(c => c + 1).
Make sure App.jsx imports MyComponent and renders <MyComponent />, and that npm run dev shows a Local: URL.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()} which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Forgetting to export MyComponent or to render <MyComponent /> in App.jsx, so the page shows nothing new.
Returning two sibling elements without wrapping them in a fragment <></> or a div.
Importing useEffect from 'react-dom' or misspelling it (useeffect).

steps.title: Update title on every render
steps.instructions: In MyComponent.jsx call useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}` }) with no dependency array so it runs after every render. Try an empty array [] to see it run only on mount, then revert.

targets.caption: Effect with no dependency array runs after every render
Side effect: update the tab title from count
Tab title updates each time you press Add

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
Two arguments: a function and an array of dependencies
No dependency array: runs on mount and every re-render
Empty dependency array: runs only once on mount
When a one-and-done effect is appropriate

hints: Import useEffect alongside useState from 'react', then call it near the top of your component.
Pass useEffect an arrow function and leave out the second argument so it runs after every render.
Inside the function set document.title to a template string like `Count: ${count}`.
To experiment, add [] as the second argument, observe the title updates only once, then remove it again.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} isn't interpolated.
Leaving the empty [] in place, so the title stops updating after mount.
Calling useEffect inside a condition or event handler instead of at the top level of the component.
Writing document.title(...) as a function call instead of assigning to it.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx pass [count] as the dependency array of the title effect. Add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: Dependency array: rerun the effect only when count changes
Copy of addCount that subtracts one
New button; clicking it also updates the tab title

explanations.topic: Putting a value in the dependency array runs the effect on mount and whenever that value changes
No dependency array means the effect runs on every re-render, even unrelated ones
Any change to count, up or down, triggers the title update

hints: The second argument to useEffect is an array; put the state value you want to watch inside it.
Write it as }, [count]); at the end of your title effect.
Copy your add function, rename it subtractCount, and use setCount(c => c - 1).
Add a <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> next to the Add button.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={subtractCount()} which calls it during render and causes an infinite loop
Leaving the dependency array empty [] so the title never updates after mount
Using setCount(count - 1) instead of the updater form c => c - 1
Copying the add function but forgetting to rename it, giving a duplicate declaration error

steps.title: Add color state as dependency
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add a color state starting at "green", a Change color button whose changeColor toggles red/green, and style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. Include color in the title and add it to the dependency array: [count, color].

targets.caption: New color state variable starting at green
Handler flips the color using the previous state
Count paragraph styled by color state
Effect reruns when count or color changes
Button that toggles red/green

explanations.topic: Toggling state with an updater function and a ternary
Inline style needs a JavaScript object, hence double curly braces
Without color in the dependency array the title ignores color changes
Effect runs whenever any value in the dependency array changes

hints: Create a second state variable with useState, initialized to "green", and use it in your effect's title string.
Write a changeColor function that calls setColor with an updater: c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green", and wire it to a button's onClick.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}: the outer braces embed JS, the inner ones make an object.
Add color to the effect's dependency array: [count, color], so the title updates when the color changes too.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to add color to the dependency array, so the title doesn't update when the color button is clicked.
Writing style={color: color} with single braces instead of style={{color: color}}.
Calling the handler immediately with onClick={changeColor()} instead of passing onClick={changeColor}.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks for the template literal, so ${color} shows literally in the title.
Forgetting to import useState or misspelling the setter (setcolor vs setColor).

steps.title: Track window size with listener
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add width and height state initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight, render them as `Window width: {width}px` and `Window height: {height}px`, and write handleResize to set both. Inside useEffect(() => {...}, []) call window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) and console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED").

targets.caption: Resize handler updates both width and height state
Listener registered inside useEffect with empty dependency array
Rendered window dimensions update as you resize

explanations.topic: State initialized from window.innerWidth/innerHeight
Adding a listener in the component body re-adds it on every render
Empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
Strict mode runs useEffect twice in development

hints: Create two state variables whose initial values come from the window object's inner size properties.
handleResize should call both setters with the current window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
Wrap window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) in useEffect so it isn't added on every render.
Pass [] as the second argument to useEffect so it runs only when the component mounts.
common_mistakes: Calling addEventListener in the component body, adding a new listener on every re-render.
Omitting the dependency array, so the effect (and listener) runs after every render.
Passing handleResize() (calling it) instead of handleResize as the callback.
Typo setheight instead of setHeight (lowercase h).
Worrying that the log appears twice: React Strict Mode runs effects twice in development.

steps.title: Return a cleanup function
steps.instructions: In the resize effect of src/MyComponent.jsx, return a function that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs EVENT LISTENER REMOVED. Refresh and check the browser console: in StrictMode it adds, removes, then adds once.

targets.caption: Cleanup removes the same resize listener
StrictMode: added, removed, then added once

explanations.topic: Returning a cleanup function from useEffect
Cleanup runs before next re-render or on unmount
Why remove event listeners: avoid unexpected behavior
StrictMode runs effect, cleans up, then runs again in development

hints: Inside the resize useEffect, after adding the listener, add a return statement that returns an arrow function.
In that returned function, undo what the effect did: call window.removeEventListener with the same event name and callback.
Pass the exact same handleResize reference you used in addEventListener, and add console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED") inside the returned function.
Refresh, open Inspect > Console: in StrictMode you should see ADDED, REMOVED, ADDED.
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener directly in the effect body instead of inside the returned function, which removes the listener immediately.
Returning the result of a call (return window.removeEventListener(...)) instead of returning a function.
Passing a new inline arrow function to removeEventListener, so it doesn't match the added handleResize and nothing is removed.
Misspelling the event name (e.g. "resized") in removeEventListener so it differs from addEventListener.
Expecting no REMOVED log in development; StrictMode intentionally runs the cleanup once on mount.

steps.title: Add second effect for title
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add another useEffect that sets document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with dependency array [width, height]. Resize the window and watch the tab title update.

targets.caption: Second useEffect updates the document title with the window size
Dependency array: rerun when width or height changes
Browser tab title shows the current size

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array [width, height] reruns the effect when size changes
Effect also runs on mount, so the title is set immediately

hints: Add a separate useEffect call below the resize one rather than putting this code in the first effect.
Inside it, assign a template string to document.title: `Size: ${width} x ${height}`.
Pass [width, height] as the second argument so it runs on mount and whenever either value changes.
Resize the browser window and look at the tab title to confirm it updates.
common_mistakes: Using normal quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} appears literally in the title
Leaving out the dependency array, so the effect runs after every render
Writing an empty dependency array [], so the title only updates once on mount
Typing document.Title or setting window.title instead of document.title
Putting the title code inside the resize effect's cleanup return
